traps.detail: A refresh token stops working if it has not been used for six months.

traps.detail: For Google Cloud Platform organizations with session control policies, sessions can be very limited (1 to 24 hours), so the app must handle re-authentication.

traps.detail: Apps in Testing with External user type get refresh tokens that expire in 7 days and are capped at 100 test users. Publishing status must be moved to In production.

traps.title: Verified scope can still show unverified warning
traps.detail: One developer reported the unverified-app warning persisting for gmail.send even after it showed as verified.

traps.title: Branding changes blocked during verification
traps.detail: Branding cannot be modified while verification is in progress, and compliant brand results expire after 7 days if unpublished.

traps.title: Changing scopes triggers re-verification
traps.detail: Moving to different sensitive or restricted scopes requires submitting for OAuth verification again.

traps.title: Refresh tokens can silently stop working
traps.detail: Tokens stop working after six months unused or when more than 100 tokens exist per account per client.

traps.title: Customer admins have the final say
traps.detail: Verification does not override Workspace admin settings; admins can mark a verified app Trusted, Limited, or Blocked.

traps.title: Callback domain can't be verified by you
traps.detail: Google requires redirect-URI domains in Authorized domains, and you cannot verify Composio's backend.composio.dev domain. Use a redirect proxy on your own domain that returns a 302 to Composio's callback.

evidence.answer: Developer report: even after gmail.send was shown as verified in the console, the 'unverified app' warning kept appearing for that scope, a blocker for end-user consent that other scopes did not hit.
